messages:
Jordan (CS): forwarding: customer@mail.com trying to use the /rerank endpoint but their client is attempting to stream results. they see a 415 and some weird scores like -inf and NaN. said it started after an SDK upgrade. pasting their snippet below.

Customer's snippet (copied):
```bash
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \n     -H 'Content-Type: text/event-stream' \n     https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank?stream=true \n     -d '{"query":"find best answer","candidates":["a","b","c"]}'
```

Customer: response HTTP/1.1 415 Unsupported Media Type, body: 'Unsupported content-type for rerank'. also some later attempts returned 200 but scores were [NaN, -inf, 0.5]. they retried in a loop and ended up with significant extra token billing.

Alex (Support): thanks jordan. can you paste the full request/response headers if they have them? also what SDK version? glad they included snippet though.

Jordan (CS): they said SDK v2.3.1 and a custom client that auto-adds `Accept: text/event-stream` when `stream=true`. no full headers yet.

Maria (Solutions Eng): quick note: rerank is not a streaming endpoint — it expects application/json POST with the query+candidates and returns synchronous scores. this will 415 on text/event-stream in many setups. also NaN/-inf suggests malformed input or candidate parse failure. we should repro. :eyes:

Tom H (Eng): agree. We saw similar before where the client sets `stream=true` globally for every call. The runtime treats rerank as non-streaming; our parser fails when content-type != application/json and falls into an error path that yields weird numeric outputs downstream.

Sahil (ML Engineer): the NaN/-inf scores smell like divide-by-zero when tokenization returns empty vectors or when candidate metadata is missing. Common causes: passing candidates as a single string with embedded JSON or sending `candidates` as a map rather than an array. Also if the `id` field is missing we try to compute alts and sometimes hit unexpected branches.

Alex (Support): ok, propose immediate steps: 1) ask customer to switch to `Content-Type: application/json` and remove `stream=true` for rerank. provide a correct cURL. 2) request logs/headers and SDK config. 3) warn about retry loop and extra billing; advise backoff and idempotency.

Maria (Solutions Eng): here's a repro they can try (and we can use locally):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"query":"which answer is best","candidates":[{"id":"a","text":"A is good"},{"id":"b","text":"B is ok"}]}'
```
Expect: 200 with JSON body containing `scores` array and stable floats.

Tom H (Eng): i'm going to repro quickly with a client that forces `Accept: text/event-stream` and `stream=true` to confirm the 415 flow and capture runtime logs. will add tracing to show where the parsing falls through.

infra-bot: New log capture session started -> session_id=logs-20260315-01.

(10m later)

Tom H (Eng): repro confirmed. When `Content-Type` != `application/json`, the request bypasses standard JSON decoder and ends up parsed as text. The rerank kernel then calls a numeric pipeline that doesn't validate candidate token vectors, leading to NaN/-inf and a 200 in some cases but with corrupt scores. When the content-type is incompatible our early validation should return 415 with a clear message; currently it sometimes returns unhelpful body or 200 with bad scores.

Sahil (ML Engineer): root cause: downstream scorer assumes token embeddings shape (N, D). If parsing fails quietly we get empty tensors and later ops produce NaN/-inf. Fixes: add strong input validation in the router (reject non-json content-type for rerank), and add NaN/inf checks before returning scores. Also sanitize SDK to not set stream=true for rerank.

Alex (Support): action items:
- [Alex] send customer the temporary mitigation cURL + ask them to stop retries and switch content-type. mention to use exponential backoff and include limits.
- [Maria] update KB article with explicit note: "/rerank does not support streaming; use application/json" and example cURL.
- [Tom] add a runtime check to reject non-json for rerank and surface an informative error (400 with message: 'rerank endpoint requires application/json; remove stream or use streaming-compatible endpoint').
- [Sahil] add NaN/inf guard and fallback score (or error) in scorer.

Jordan (CS): i've messaged the customer with the cURL above and asked them to stop the loop. they confirmed they switched headers and saw a clean 200 with sensible scores. they also said billing team noticed extra charges; asked for an invoice credit.

Alex (Support): escalated billing request to finance, included request id and session logs. flagged for intent: accidental repeated retries. recommend credit for obvious client bug.

Maria (Solutions Eng): will draft doc edits and a short note in the SDK release notes to prevent global `stream=true` toggles.

Tom H (Eng): created PR to add content-type validation + better error message; linking -> PR #4123. also added telemetry to detect clients passing `stream=true` to non-stream endpoints.

Sahil (ML Engineer): added unit test to ensure scorers return explicit error on NaN/inf instead of propagating.

Alex (Support): leaving this open until finance replies on credit. customer confirmed workaround works. closing once billing resolved. :white_check_mark:

Jordan (CS): customer also asked for a small note we can add to the support portal explaining "why rerank is not streamable" — maria, can you include a one-liner?

Maria (Solutions Eng): one-liner: "Rerank is a synchronous scoring operation that returns a fixed array of scores for a provided list of candidates — streaming responses are not supported because scoring must finish before stable ranks can be emitted."

infra-bot: Ticket updated: TICKET-8891, linked logs session=logs-20260315-01, PR=4123.

Alex (Support): marking internal resolution steps done. will follow-up with finance and update customer.

Jordan (CS): thanks team. good catch on the SDK behaviour.

(End of thread)
